definition: Finetuned Language Net — Google’s instruction-tuning recipe that fine-tunes LMs on hundreds of tasks phrased as instructions, sharply improving zero-shot generalization.
details: Finetuned Language Net — Google’s instruction-tuning recipe that fine-tunes LMs on hundreds of tasks phrased as instructions, sharply improving zero-shot generalization.

explainer.lead: FLAN is Google’s recipe for teaching language models to follow instructions by fine-tuning them on hundreds of differently phrased tasks. The goal is a model that can handle a new task from its instruction alone, without being shown task-specific examples first.

tiers.eli5: Imagine practising many kinds of schoolwork, with every exercise written as a clear instruction. After enough practice, you may understand a new kind of exercise just by reading what it asks you to do. FLAN gives language models similar practice across hundreds of tasks.
tiers.practitioner: Apply FLAN by converting examples from many tasks into instruction-based inputs and fine-tuning a language model on the resulting mixture. Its purpose is zero-shot generalization, so evaluate it on tasks the model can attempt from instructions alone rather than only on the fine-tuning tasks. Keep in mind that FLAN describes a training recipe, not a particular model architecture.
tiers.paperLevel: FLAN fine-tunes a language model on a mixture of hundreds of tasks, with each task expressed as instructions. Formally, training examples from many tasks are mapped to instruction-based text pairs, and the resulting mixture is used for supervised fine-tuning to improve zero-shot performance on new tasks.

explainer.example: During fine-tuning, the model might practise instructions such as “Translate this sentence into French” and “Summarize this paragraph.” It could then receive the unseen instruction “Classify this review as positive or negative: The battery lasts all day” and answer “Positive” without being shown labelled reviews first.

usedIn.name: Google language-model training
usedIn.detail: FLAN is Google’s instruction-tuning recipe for fine-tuning language models on hundreds of tasks.

usedIn.name: Zero-shot language tasks
usedIn.detail: The approach is used to improve a model’s ability to generalize to tasks presented only through instructions.

explainer.intuition: A model that practises many tasks in a common instruction format can learn to interpret the instruction itself, rather than memorizing one fixed task. That shared practice is what supports better performance on unseen tasks.
howItWorks: Collect training examples spanning hundreds of language tasks.
Phrase the examples as instructions so different tasks share a consistent instruction-following setup.
Fine-tune a language model on this mixture of instruction-based tasks.
Give the tuned model an instruction for a new task and let it respond without task-specific examples.
explainer.whyItMatters: FLAN makes language models more useful when a requested task was not individually prepared during training. Its instruction-based fine-tuning sharply improves zero-shot generalization.
misconceptions: FLAN is a fine-tuning recipe, not a neural-network architecture.
Zero-shot does not mean the model received no training; it means no examples of the new task are supplied at request time.
Instruction tuning is more than writing a single clever prompt because it changes the model through fine-tuning.
